thread:
incident-bot: Pager: SEV-2 — widespread SRV lookup timeouts from control plane to service discovery in az1c. Trigger: >5% 5xx on internal service registry and multiple consumer jobs failing SRV lookups. Auto-page to #incidents and oncall.
opsbot: Paging @anna (on-call) and @devon. See alert group: srv-lookup-errors.az1c. Incident channel created.
anna: I'm on it, grabbing context. quick status: is this isolated to az1c only?
devon: seeing SRV failures from az1c -> consul backend, also CoreDNS returning SERVFAIL intermittently. az1a/az1b look normal so far.
marta: I can confirm increased 5xx rate from the model-serving control plane in az1c. Telemetry: avg SRV latency spiked from 15ms -> 800ms, then timeouts.
raj: logs from consul cluster show gRPC timeouts and slow raft heartbeats for members in az1c.
jules: customer impact: two enterprise customers see deploys failing and feature flag evals blocked; CI runners in az1c failing tests. No external customer API errors yet but internal orchestration affected.
anna: ok. immediate mitigation plan: 1) find and isolate the root of DNS egress/backplane saturation 2) failover traffic for control-plane service discovery to az1a fallback 3) restore stable SRV responses. assigning tasks.
anna: @devon take routing/failover (BGP/route tables), @marta look at CoreDNS/consul pods in az1c, @raj examine consul raft/peers, @jules coordinate comms and impact.
devon: On it. checking VPC peering and NAT gateways for az1c. early hypothesis: egress NAT queue buildup due to recent regional peering change.
netops-bot: Noted BGP flap at 2026-03-15T10:04:12Z between AZ1C transit-router and peer-asn 64512. 3 withdraws, 2 reannounces.
marta: kubectl from az1c control plane:
```
$ kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep coredns
coredns-7f8b9c6d-1   1/1   Running   2 (10m ago)   10.5.1.12   az1c
coredns-7f8b9c6d-2   0/1   CrashLoopBackOff  4 (3m ago)   10.5.1.13   az1c
```
marta: CoreDNS logs:
```
2026-03-15T10:07:03Z [ERROR] plugin/forward: read udp 10.5.1.12:55234->10.0.0.53:53: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T10:07:04Z [WARN] failed to forward request: dial tcp 10.0.0.53:53: connect: connection refused
```
raj: consul logs from one az1c member:
```
2026-03-15T10:05:58Z [WARN] rpc: dial tcp 10.5.2.21:8300: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T10:06:12Z [ERR] raft: failed to send to peer: send failed
```
anna: so both DNS forwarders and consul RPC egress are experiencing timeouts -> points to egress path saturation or blackholing.
devon: I pushed a temporary route policy to steer control-plane egress from az1c to az1a NAT gateway for service discovery IP ranges (10.0.0.0/22). Will monitor.
opsbot: route-change: added route 10.0.0.0/22 -> nat-gw-az1a for az1c (policy id r-az1c-20260315-1) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
marta: after reroute, CoreDNS forward attempts reduced, still seeing a few timeouts but overall SRV latency dropping.
anna: perform the kube-level mitigation too: scale coredns in az1c to 4 replicas and restart the crashloop pod.
marta: applied:
```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=4 --context=az1c
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment coredns --context=az1c
```
marta: coredns pods are stabilizing, forward errors gone on new pods.
raj: forcing consul member to leave and rejoin to fix raft partitioning for az1c.
```
consul leave -address=10.5.2.21
consul join 10.5.1.10
```
raj: after rejoin, raft heartbeats recovered, queries to consul succeed.
devon: BGP peer is still unstable; netops tracing shows peer interface dropping packets when egress queue > 95% for flows to our NAT. we're investigating with provider.
netops-bot: Provider case opened: ticket #PR-44912 created with transit provider. ETA initial response 20 mins.
jules: customer-impact update: two customers had failures in CI and deploys between 10:05-10:18 UTC. We sent initial heads-up to account contacts. No data loss, only orchestration failures.
anna: runbook follow-ups: - keep reroute until provider confirms stabilisation - keep coredns scaled for 30m - enable canary control-plane traffic back to az1c only when BGP stable for 10m - postmortem assignment: raj/marta/devon
marta: quick smoke check for services that use SRV: `nslookup -type=SRV _grpc._tcp.service-registry.internal 10.5.1.12` now returns consistent answers.
anna: monitoring: set temporary alert to trigger if SRV error rate >1% for next 2 hours and page on call.
opsbot: Alert threshold updated (srv-lookup-errors.az1c) -> page @anna @devon
devon: provider responded: they had a misconfigured queue policy that interacted poorly with our burst from peering changes; they applied a fix at 10:24 UTC. BGP flaps stopped shortly after (10:25).
raj: rolling back route policy to original now that provider fixed egress. removing r-az1c-20260315-1
opsbot: route-change: removed r-az1c-20260315-1 :white_check_mark:
marta: coredns replicas scaled back to 2 and deployment stabilized.
```
kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=2 --context=az1c
```
jules: customer comms: follow-up note sent with timeline and ETA for postmortem. support tickets triaged to high priority.
anna: current status: degraded window 10:04-10:25 UTC. SRV errors resolved, consul raft healthy, BGP stable.
anna: incident severity downgraded to SEV-3. we'll keep channel open for postmortem notes. Great job coordinating everyone. :clap:
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=resolved (mitigated), severity=3, assignees=[raj,marta,devon], postmortem-due=2026-03-22.
